method: Wave-5 extends the lifecycle corpus across naming NFTs, breedable collectibles, metaverse land, interactive Bitcoin Ordinals and a terminal centralized marketplace. Primary operator, protocol and public-company filings anchor claims. A live interface establishes operation, not demand; a registration count is not holder count; fixed sub-series supply is not family-wide supply; current sale prices are not historical mint prices; and platform inventory is not collection supply.

profile.launched: ENS first names were minted in 2017. The reviewed first-party launch history identifies the year but not a single day, so no false date precision is added.
profile.supply: No fixed collection cap: names are created within a hierarchical namespace and registrations expire or renew. ENS reported more than 1.5 million registered names in February 2026, but that operator snapshot is not treated as current active names, unique owners or a fixed NFT supply.
profile.mint_price: Current .eth registration fees vary by length: $5/year for names of at least five characters, $160/year for four characters and $640/year for three characters, paid in ETH, with temporary premiums after expiry. This recurring pricing is not a universal historical mint price or audited aggregate raise; fees go to the ENS Treasury.
profile.community_history: ENS evolved from a 2017 Ethereum naming system into tokenholder governance, working groups, grants and multichain primary-name support. Governance participation and registration totals are not converted into active-community or holder-retention claims.
profile.founder_engagement: Nick Johnson founded and led ENS. Current responsibilities span ENS Labs, the ENS DAO and the ENS Foundation; the Foundation names Nick Johnson, Kevin Gaspar and Alex Van de Sande as directors.
profile.benefits: Names can resolve human-readable identifiers to addresses and records, provide primary identity, create subnames and participate in ENS governance where token rights apply. No appreciation, yield, universal-wallet support or permanent ownership without renewal is promised.
profile.business: Registration and renewal fees flow to the ENS Treasury, while governance allocates resources and grants. The reviewed sources do not disclose name-level profitability, current protocol costs or a clean NFT-holder revenue entitlement.
profile.analysis: Thriving means active 2026 protocol architecture, governance, security stewardship and multichain product work. It does not establish secondary-market liquidity, holder concentration, registration retention, treasury profitability or investment returns.

team.control_boundary: Protocol development, token governance and legal representation are distributed across separate bodies.

chronology.event: The first ENS names were minted on Ethereum.
ENS introduced tokenholder DAO governance.
ENS published the ENSv2 architecture and reported more than 1.5 million registered names.
ENS announced a new Security Council as current protocol stewardship continued.

market_holder_boundaries.market: No current floor, secondary volume, bid depth, liquidity or realized-return series.
market_holder_boundaries.holders: No current unique-owner, concentration, renewal-retention or active-user count; registrations can expire and one address can control many names.
market_holder_boundaries.available_evidence: Operator registration totals and live governance establish scale and operation, not holder quality or market health.

products_and_value_capture.capture: Registration and renewal fees fund the treasury; no name-owner cash flow or audited protocol margin is asserted.

why.finding: Renewable naming utility, composable records and governance provide a use case beyond collectible imagery. Current development supports continuity, but the evidence does not isolate utility's effect on price or retention.

strategic_choices.choice: Represent .eth second-level ownership as NFTs while preserving a hierarchical naming system.
Use recurring length-based pricing and expiry premiums rather than one fixed mint.
Distribute governance and stewardship across a DAO, Labs, Foundation and Security Council.

counterfactual.finding: Without continuing resolver, wallet and governance support, names could remain tokens but lose practical identity utility. Current multichain and security work reduces that risk without proving adoption or financial performance.

risks.risk: Renewal and expiry mean registration snapshots can overstate durable ownership.
Architecture and wrapper transitions can create compatibility, governance and security complexity.
Naming utility depends on resolver, application and wallet integration beyond token ownership.

unknowns: Current active and renewed names by namespace.
Current unique owners, concentration and secondary-market liquidity.
Treasury revenue, costs and profitability attributable to registrations.
Adoption and failure rates for current L2 primary-name integrations.

evidence.value: First ENS names minted in 2017; exact day withheld
Dynamic namespace without fixed cap; February 2026 operator snapshot exceeds 1.5 million names
Current recurring .eth pricing varies by length; historical universal mint and aggregate raise not applicable
thriving — current protocol, governance and security work verified; not market performance
DAO, working groups and grants documented; participation and retention withheld
Nick Johnson founded ENS; current stewardship split among named organizations
Naming, records, primary identity, subnames and governance without financial promises
Registration fees flow to treasury; holder revenue and protocol profitability withheld
Current operational continuity verified; market, retention and financial conclusions withheld

profile.launched: CryptoKitties launched in 2017 at Axiom Zen, before Dapper Labs was founded and spun out in 2018. The dossier preserves that corporate chronology rather than retroactively assigning the launch to a later company.
profile.supply: Dynamic breedable supply, not a fixed 10k collection. Dapper currently reports more than 2 million CryptoKitties; the 50,000 cap applies only to Generation 0, while later generations are created through breeding. Neither figure is a current holder count.
profile.mint_price: No single universal mint: Generation 0 used sales and the system also uses marketplace purchase, breeding and siring. The reviewed first-party sources do not provide a defensible original average price or aggregate raise, so both are withheld.
profile.community_history: The project introduced collection, breeding and trading loops to a broad consumer audience and Dapper reports more than 400,000 historical players. Current related product ALL THE ZEN continued events in 2026, but its player telemetry is not treated as activity in the original Ethereum collection.
profile.founder_engagement: CryptoKitties originated at Axiom Zen. Dapper Labs, founded by Roham Gharegozlou and Dieter Shirley in 2018, is the current corporate steward and continues to list CryptoKitties and operate related experiences.
profile.benefits: Owners can collect, breed, sell, make offers and offer cats for siring; genetic attributes affect offspring and Fancy Cat combinations. Benefits require Ethereum transactions and parts of the presentation remain website-dependent; no yield or price guarantee exists.
profile.business: The original loop combined primary distribution, marketplace trading, breeding and siring. Current collection-specific fee revenue, Dapper costs and ALL THE ZEN economics are not disclosed in the reviewed sources.
profile.analysis: Thriving means Dapper continues to present the original product, its API and guide remain available, and a related CryptoKitties experience ran a February 2026 event. It does not establish original-collection volume, active breeders, unique holders, fee revenue or profitability.

team.control_boundary: The original Ethereum assets and newer ALL THE ZEN experience are related but analytically distinct.

chronology.event: Axiom Zen launched CryptoKitties on Ethereum.
The Kitty Clock stopped producing Generation 0 cats after 34,928 clock cats; reserved/event cats remained within the 50,000 Gen0 cap.
Dapper launched the related ALL THE ZEN CryptoKitties experience.
ALL THE ZEN announced a Lucky Golden Event, providing current operator evidence for continued franchise activity.

market_holder_boundaries.market: No current original-collection floor, volume, bid depth, breeding activity, siring revenue or liquidity.
market_holder_boundaries.holders: No current unique-holder or concentration series; Dapper's historical player count and related-game users are not Ethereum NFT owners.
market_holder_boundaries.available_evidence: Current product surfaces and aggregate creation/player milestones establish continuity and historical reach, not market health.

products_and_value_capture.capture: Potential transaction and product economics are visible, but current collection-level revenue and costs are withheld.

why.finding: Genetic breeding and visible ancestry created a repeatable participation loop beyond static ownership. Continued stewardship supports durability, but dynamic supply and legacy UX can weaken scarcity and participation.

strategic_choices.choice: Make later-generation supply user-created through breeding rather than fixing total supply.
Combine collection, marketplace, offers and siring inside one game loop.
Extend the franchise through ALL THE ZEN while retaining the original Ethereum product and API.

counterfactual.finding: Without breeding and genetic differentiation, CryptoKitties would lose its core participatory mechanic. Without maintained interfaces, some website-rendered traits and mainstream usability would degrade even if tokens persisted.

risks.risk: Breedable supply can expand independently of unique-user growth.
Fancy Cat appearance depends partly on the official website rather than only token data.
Current activity in ALL THE ZEN cannot be assumed to create liquidity or users for original Ethereum cats.

unknowns: Original average purchase price and audited aggregate primary proceeds.
Current unique owners, concentration, floor, volume and active breeders.
Current marketplace, breeding and siring fee revenue.
Conversion or overlap between original NFT owners and ALL THE ZEN users.

evidence.value: 2017 launch at Axiom Zen; Dapper founded in 2018
More than 2 million dynamic cats; 50,000 cap applies only to Generation 0
No universal mint; original average and aggregate proceeds withheld
thriving — original resources and a February 2026 related product event verified; not original-market health
Historical reach and current related-product activity documented; original-holder retention withheld
Axiom Zen origin and Dapper stewardship documented with corporate chronology preserved
Collection, breeding, selling, offers and siring without financial promises
Marketplace, breeding and related product loops; current collection economics withheld
Continuing stewardship verified; original market, holder and financial conclusions withheld

profile.launched: The Sandbox's first blockchain LAND presales began in 2019. Current official sales use Polygon; the dossier distinguishes original Ethereum-era land from later Polygon sale infrastructure.
profile.supply: 166,464 LAND parcels, with operator documentation stating no new LAND can be created. Estates bundle parcels and do not increase underlying supply; marketplace listings and sale inventory are not holder counts.
profile.mint_price: Pricing varied across presales and sales, so there is no universal historical mint price in the reviewed sources. The current July 2026 sale listed Standard LAND at 1,011 SAND and Premium LAND at 4,683 SAND; those catalog prices are not historical averages or an aggregate raise.
profile.community_history: LAND moved from presales into an open creator-publishing world with experiences, events and owner building. Current sale and documentation prove continued operation, but not active-owner retention, visitors or profitable land use.
profile.founder_engagement: Arthur Madrid and Sébastien Borget are identified as co-founders and current CEO and COO. The Sandbox and its Foundation operate the world, creator economics and current LAND sales.
profile.benefits: LAND can host experiences, games and assets, be combined into Estates, transferred or monetized through creator activity. Scarcity, adjacency and publishing rights do not guarantee traffic, rent, yield or appreciation.
profile.business: The Sandbox combines LAND sales, creator publishing and marketplace economics. Official materials state creators receive 95% and the Foundation 5% in the described model, but that split is not a standardized LAND-owner cash flow or current audited margin.
profile.analysis: Thriving means an active July 2026 official sale, live owner documentation and an operating creator world. It does not establish LAND floor, secondary volume, occupancy, visitor demand, unique owners, rental income or profitability.

chronology.event: The first LAND presales began under the blockchain-world roadmap.
The Sandbox documented the fixed 166,464 LAND supply and creator economics.
The world opened user-generated experience publishing.
A current official Polygon LAND sale opened with 990 Standard parcels and disclosed catalog prices.

market_holder_boundaries.market: No current floor, secondary volume, bids, liquidity, rent, occupancy or realized-return series.
market_holder_boundaries.holders: No current unique-owner, concentration, active-builder or retention count; current sale inventory is not holder telemetry.
market_holder_boundaries.available_evidence: Fixed supply and a current operator sale establish scarcity design and operation, not market strength.

products_and_value_capture.capture: LAND sales and creator/ Foundation fees are documented; current LAND revenue, creator earnings and owner returns are withheld.

why.finding: Fixed parcel supply, location and creator publishing give LAND functional differentiation. Continued sales and tooling support continuity, while current demand and productive use remain unproven.

strategic_choices.choice: Fix total LAND at 166,464 and represent Estates as bundles rather than new parcels.
Open experience publishing to creators rather than limit content to the operator.
Move official LAND sales to Polygon and require KYC for primary purchases.

counterfactual.finding: Without usable publishing and visitors, fixed land would remain scarce coordinates without productive utility. Current creator tools and sales reduce abandonment risk but do not prove occupancy or returns.

risks.risk: Fixed supply does not guarantee active experiences, visitors, rental demand or liquidity.
Ethereum-to-Polygon infrastructure and KYC create migration and access dependencies.
Current primary-sale prices can be mistaken for secondary fair value or historical mint price.

unknowns: Realized average price and aggregate proceeds across historical LAND presales.
Current unique owners, concentration, floor, volume and bid depth.
Active scenes, visitors, occupancy, rentals and creator earnings attributable to LAND.
Unsold operator/Foundation inventory and its future release schedule.

triggers: new owner, usage or revenue disclosure

evidence.value: First LAND presales began in 2019
166,464 fixed parcels; Estates do not create new LAND
Historical prices varied; July 2026 catalog lists 1,011 and 4,683 SAND, not historical averages
thriving — current Polygon sale and creator infrastructure verified; not demand or market performance
Creator publishing and current sale continuity documented; active-owner retention withheld
Arthur Madrid and Sébastien Borget identified as co-founders and current executives
Building, publishing, transfer and monetization functions without yield promises
LAND sales and creator economy documented; current owner economics withheld
Operation verified; market, holder, occupancy and financial conclusions withheld

profile.launched: Pizza Ninjas V1 launched by 2024 as an interactive recursive Ordinals collection. The reviewed official design documents do not state an exact launch day, so this dossier avoids false precision and separates V1 from a later advertised mint.
profile.supply: Exactly 1,500 V1 Pizza Ninjas under the project parent inscription. The current official site advertises a November 25, 2025 mint but does not disclose that later edition's supply; 1,500 is therefore not represented as a family-wide total.
profile.mint_price: Official V1 documentation describes a 300-custom-Ninja presale selection process but does not state the mint price or audited proceeds. The later official site also omits a price, so no universal mint or aggregate raise is asserted.
profile.community_history: V1 used community-created custom Ninjas and a video competition for mint access. A current official site remains online, but its primary call-to-action still references a past November 2025 mint; this does not establish current holder retention or delivery.
profile.founder_engagement: The provenance document identifies founder inscription #1085 by the pseudonymous handle @TO and Ninjalerts as the parent company. Eight participating artists are described but not individually identified in the reviewed first-party materials.
profile.benefits: Each V1 Ninja is designed as a JavaScript application with customization, animation, stickers and an onchain SNES emulator; holders can opt into upgrades through reinscription. No perpetual hosting, game availability, yield or appreciation is promised.
profile.business: The project combines Ordinals collection sales, Ninjalerts tooling and interactive media. Price, proceeds, royalties, current company ownership and project-level revenue remain undisclosed.
profile.analysis: Middling means V1 provenance and interactive design are documented and an official site remains live, while the live surface still promotes a past mint and does not verify current delivery, usage or community activity. It does not establish floor, volume, holders, product usage or revenue.

team.artists: Eight artists/enthusiasts described but not named in the reviewed primary pages
team.scope_boundary: V1's documented 1,500 inscriptions are separated from the later advertised mint.

chronology.event: V1 launched with 1,500 interactive recursive Pizza Ninjas; exact day is not stated in reviewed official documentation.
The project documented 300 custom Ninja presale selections and a curated generative-art process.
The official site advertised a later mint for this date without disclosing supply or price.
The official site and design documentation remained available, but the site still surfaced the past mint call-to-action.

market_holder_boundaries.market: No current floor, volume, bids, liquidity, royalty or realized-return series.
market_holder_boundaries.holders: No current unique-holder, concentration, retention or interactive-usage count.
market_holder_boundaries.available_evidence: Fixed V1 supply and a live official surface establish provenance and preservation, not market or community health.

products_and_value_capture.capture: Collection and tooling channels exist, but price, fees, royalties, revenue and current usage are withheld.

why.finding: Treating each inscription as an interactive application differentiates the project from static PFPs. The same recursive execution and upgrade design adds dependency, fragmentation and preservation risk.

strategic_choices.choice: Build V1 as 1,500 JavaScript applications under a parent inscription.
Use community customs and a video competition to allocate some mint access.
Make upgrades holder-opt-in through reinscription and limit emulator ROMs to claimed public-domain works.

counterfactual.finding: Without recursive interactive functions, Pizza Ninjas would be a smaller static PFP thesis. Without maintained execution dependencies, some application features could degrade even while the base inscriptions persist.

risks.risk: V1 and later-mint marketing can blur supply and lifecycle scope.
Recursive JavaScript and browser execution add dependencies beyond base image inscription.
Opt-in upgrades can fragment versions; emulator content also carries rights risk despite the project's public-domain policy.

unknowns: Exact V1 launch day, mint price and aggregate proceeds.
Supply, price, delivery status and relationship of the November 2025 advertised mint to V1.
Current unique holders, concentration, floor, volume and liquidity.
Current interactive-feature usage, Ninjalerts revenue and named artist roster.

triggers: new primary holder or market telemetry

evidence.value: V1 launched by 2024; exact day withheld
1,500 V1 inscriptions; later advertised mint supply unknown
V1 presale process documented; price and aggregate proceeds withheld
middling — official surface remains but dated mint messaging does not verify current delivery or activity
Custom-art and video-competition participation documented; current retention withheld
@TO and Ninjalerts identified; legal identity and full artist roster withheld
Interactive customization, animation, stickers, emulator and opt-in upgrades without financial promises
Collection and tooling model visible; current fees and revenue withheld
Provenance and live surface verified; delivery, market, holder and usage conclusions withheld

profile.launched: Nifty Gateway launched in 2020 after Gemini acquired the pre-launch company in November 2019. Acquisition and product launch are separate lifecycle milestones.
profile.supply: Not applicable: Nifty Gateway was a custodial marketplace and digital-production platform spanning many creators and drops, not one NFT collection. Listed inventory, drops and users must not be represented as token supply or holder count.
profile.mint_price: Not applicable as a platform-wide mint. Individual drops used different prices and sale formats; the reviewed primary sources do not provide an audited platform-wide average mint price or aggregate creator proceeds.
profile.community_history: The platform combined curated drops, fiat payments, custodial wallets and a secondary marketplace. Gemini placed it in withdrawal-only mode on January 23, 2026 and closed the platform on February 23, 2026.
profile.founder_engagement: Gemini identifies twin brothers Duncan and Griffin as the founders and acquired Nifty Gateway in 2019. Gemini later operated the platform and made the closure decision; no standalone post-closure operating team is asserted.
profile.benefits: Before closure, users could access curated creator drops, fiat payment methods, custodial wallets and secondary listings. Those platform services ended; withdrawal and tax-support documentation does not make the marketplace operational.
profile.business: Nifty Gateway operated curated primary drops, production services and secondary transactions. Gemini said closure would concentrate resources on a one-stop super app and later reported that it had wound down Nifty Gateway; collection-level revenue, losses and creator payouts are not disclosed here.
profile.analysis: Dead is anchored to Gemini's explicit February 23, 2026 closure and March 2026 public-company confirmation that Nifty Gateway was wound down. This is a platform terminal outcome, not a claim that underlying NFTs ceased to exist or that every creator project failed.

team.post_closure_boundary: Gemini Wallet may support NFTs, but it is not continuation of the Nifty Gateway marketplace.

chronology.event: Gemini acquired the pre-launch Nifty Gateway company.
Nifty Gateway launched as an NFT platform.
Gemini put the platform into withdrawal-only mode and announced a February 23 closure.
Nifty Gateway closed; Gemini's March 2026 filing subsequently confirmed it had been wound down.

market_holder_boundaries.market: No current marketplace floor, volume, bid depth or liquidity because the platform closed.
market_holder_boundaries.holders: Not a collection: users, custodial accounts, creators and owners of underlying NFTs are different populations, and no current count is asserted.
market_holder_boundaries.available_evidence: Operator closure and public-company wind-down confirmation establish terminal platform status, not the status or value of underlying assets.

products_and_value_capture.capture: Historical platform economics existed across drops and trades, but audited Nifty-specific revenue, loss, fees and creator payouts are withheld.

why.finding: Gemini explicitly framed closure as resource concentration around its one-stop super app. A prior filing documented commercial-viability risk, but this dossier does not promote that general risk into an unsupported sole cause.

strategic_choices.choice: Use Gemini ownership, fiat payments and custodial wallets to reduce purchase friction.
Pair curated drops with production services and a secondary marketplace.
Enter withdrawal-only mode before closure and redirect NFT support toward Gemini Wallet.

counterfactual.finding: A sale or independent operating model might have preserved the marketplace, but the reviewed primary sources do not say one was pursued. Gemini instead chose wind-down and product concentration.

risks.risk: Custodial users faced withdrawal and self-custody work before shutdown.
Platform closure can strand interfaces and community coordination even when underlying blockchain assets persist.
Gemini had disclosed that weak NFT demand or volume could make the business commercially nonviable, but exact closure economics remain undisclosed.

unknowns: Nifty Gateway-specific revenue, losses and closure costs.
Number and value of assets withdrawn, migrated or left unresolved at closure.
Creator payout and support obligations remaining after shutdown.
Whether any Nifty technology, staff or IP continues inside Gemini products.

evidence.value: 2020 platform launch after Gemini's 2019 acquisition
Not applicable to a multi-creator marketplace platform
Not applicable platform-wide; drop formats varied and aggregate proceeds withheld
dead — platform closed 2026-02-23 and Gemini subsequently confirmed wind-down
Curated platform entered withdrawal-only mode and then closed; underlying NFTs are outside terminal claim
Founders and Gemini acquisition documented; Gemini made the closure decision
Historical drops, fiat, custody and secondary market ended with closure
Resource-concentration rationale and wind-down verified; exact economics withheld
Terminal marketplace outcome verified; underlying asset and creator outcomes bounded separately
